title: Lecture 8 · The Ant System
outline:
Lecture 8 video (Nature-Inspired Computation, ECM3412): 'The Ant System'. 11 scenes, 120.5 s: title (4), the loop (11), one ant builds a tour (12), score every road (12.5), roll the dice (9), the dials alpha and beta (12), evaporate then deposit (12.5), positive feedback / the snowball (12.5), who deposits: Ant System, Elitist rank, Max-Min (12.5), construction graphs: scheduling (13.5), recap (9). Story: the Ant System is a loop of three steps (place ants on random towns, every ant builds a whole tour with the transition rule, update the trails), repeated until an end condition; the ants forget (tabu lists reset), the trails remember (scenes 2-3, lesson 8.1). To pick its next town an ant at town i scores every town j it may still visit with trail^alpha x closeness^beta, where closeness = 1/d; a visited town (tabu list) scores zero; the scores are divided by their total to give chances, and a roulette draw turns the chances into a choice (scenes 4-5, lesson 8.2); alpha and beta set how much the ants trust the trail and closeness: alpha 0 = nearest wins, beta 0 = strongest trail wins (scene 6). The update rule is new trail = (1 - rho) x old trail + the sum of Q/L over the ants that used the road: evaporate, then deposit, shorter tours lay more (scene 7, lesson 8.3); the positive feedback this creates snowballs a good round (scene 8, lesson 8.3). Variants change who deposits: all ants (Ant System), the best 3 (Elitist Rank), the best 1 (Max-Min): more focus, more trail on the best round, but more colonies stuck on a poor round (scene 9, lesson 8.4). The same ideas solve any problem whose solutions are paths in a graph: a one-press print shop, each job a node, the ant starts at Start, the schedule's lateness is the fitness (scene 10, lesson 8.5). Not covered: the early-results table against GA and annealing, Q as pure scale, layered graphs (the dinner menu), the boss quiz; the recap points to Workshop 8.W.

LESSONS the facts come from: l8-loop 8.1, l8-transition 8.2, l8-update 8.3, l8-variants 8.4, l8-schedule 8.5, l8-wlab 8.W; js/content/nic/l8-01.js .. l8-03.js, l8-workshop.js, boss-nic-78.js; bank js/bank/nic-46.js and nic-47.js.

IDEA: one round of the Ant System is three steps: (1) put the ants on random towns, (2) every ant builds a whole tour, (3) update the trails. Then the loop repeats: the ants start afresh but the trails stay, so the trails are the colony's memory. Run for real: three ants on the five villages P Q R S T, round 1 from equal trails, round 2 starting from the updated trails. Graph: const ang = (k) => ((-90 + k * 72) * Math.PI) / 180; const nodes = {Start: {x: 110, y: 150, w: 130, label: 'Start'}}; [...L8.JOB_IDS].forEach((j, k) => (nodes[j] = [590 + 190 * Math.cos(ang(k)), 150 + 120 * Math.sin(ang(k))])) (B top, then L, P, T, W clockwise; W ends up on the left near Start); const net = L8.net(stage, {nodes, edges: [], r: 34, fs: 40}) (no base roads: draw only paths). Tag L8.tag(stage, {x: 0, y: 10, text: 'one press, five jobs', tone: 'grey'}). Ant: const ant = L5.svg(stage).appendChild(L8.ant(0, 0, 70)), placed with net.rest('Start') and net.walk(from, to, f) (from / to are 'Start' or a job letter). Schedule chart: const g = L8.gantt(stage, {x: 43, y: 330, order: L8.SCHED.order}) (blocks 5 px per minute: 170 min = 850 px; under each block 'ends N', 'due N' and a late tag; total height 206). Stats: L8.stat(stage, {x: 0, y: 548, w: 440, h: 80, label: 'average lateness', tone: 'red'}) and L8.stat(stage, {x: 480, y: 548, w: 440, h: 80, label: 'maximum lateness', tone: 'red'}).

DATA (L8.SCHED, L8.JOBS, L8.evalOrder, asserted in common-2.js; lesson 8.5): jobs (duration, due) B 30/100, L 30/20, P 30/50, T 30/80, W 50/30. L8.SCHED.steps[k] = {at, J, to}: the real run (rng 2, alpha = beta = 1, eta = 100 / due) picks W (from Start, J = B L P T W), then L (J = B L P T), then P (J = B P T), then T (J = B T), then B (J = B only): L8.SCHED.order = 'WLPTB' (W is picked first although L is due sooner: the choice is a weighted random draw). L8.SCHED.eval.rows: W ends 50 due 30 late 20; L ends 80 due 20 late 60; P ends 110 due 50 late 60; T ends 140 due 80 late 60; B ends 170 due 100 late 70; average lateness 54 (270 / 5), maximum 70. Assert in build(): L8.same(L8.SCHED.order, 'WLPTB', ...), L8.same(L8.SCHED.eval.avg, 54, ...), L8.same(L8.SCHED.eval.max, 70, ...).

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.0 the five job nodes pop (0.1 s apart) and the Start node pops (purple: nodes {Start: {tone: 'purple'}}); 0.8 the tag pops; 1.6-2.2 the ant pops on Start (net.rest('Start')). STEPS k = 0..4 start at s = 3.2 + 1.2 k (3.2, 4.4, 5.6, 6.8, 8.0): s + 0.0-0.4 thin grey arrows pop from the current node to every job still allowed (paths: J.map((j) => ({a: from, b: j, k, tone: 'grey', w: 4, head: true}))); s + 0.4-0.7 the chosen one turns orange and thick (w 10) while the other arrows fade out (o 1 -> 0); s + 0.6-1.1 the ant hops to the chosen job (net.walk, E.inOut); s + 0.9-1.3 that job's node turns red (visited, tone 'red') and its block grows into the chart from the left (g.update({n: k + ramp}) with n counting up 0 -> 5; blocks are grey until the lateness beat). 9.3-9.9 the chart's 'ends' and 'due' lines fade in (dueK 0 -> 1): lateness = finish time minus due time can be read off each block. 10.0-11.0 the late tags pop (lateK 0 -> 1) and the blocks turn red: late 20, 60, 60, 60, 70. 11.3-12.0 the two stat stickers pop: average lateness 54, maximum lateness 70 (bump). 12.0-13.5 hold.

helpers:
FILES: videos/l8/common.js (pure data and algorithms, no DOM: the real rules on lecture 8's own data, every storyboard number asserted at load), common-2.js (data part 2: the ten-village colony, the three update rules, the print shop), common-3.js (drawing basics: tags, chips, stats, discs, tokens, cards, labels, the ant icon, arithmetic signs, L8.fit / L8.along / L8.seq), common-4.js (the map: L8.net), common-5.js (strip, bar, dial, gantt). Everything hangs off window.VID.l8; scenes start with const V = window.VID, L8 = V.l8, L5 = V.l5 and const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. videos/lecture-8.html loads engine.js, cards.js, l5/common.js (for L5: tick, cross, arrow, dice, drawOn, svg, badge, tone), then l8/common.js ... common-5.js, then scene-01 ... scene-11, audio/lecture-8.js. l6 is not loaded. Every helper file starts with a long API comment listing every signature, option and return value: READ THEM FIRST, they are the contract. All draw calls are pure: call them every frame from update(t) with everything you want to see; nothing is remembered between frames; no Math.random, Date or timers.

A. DATA (common.js, common-2.js): L8.rng, L8.same / L8.close (throw clear Errors), L8.score / shares / pick (the transition rule and the roulette), L8.FIVE {ids, xy, d, key, edges, tau}, L8.antTour, L8.ONE (the lesson's ant, tour TPQRS, 74 km), L8.LOOP (three ants, two rounds), L8.HUB (Ash / Birch / Cedar / Dale, scores, chances, draws), L8.COURIER + L8.dials + L8.DIAL {balanced, greedy, trail}, L8.LEDGER + L8.nextTau, L8.TEN {names, xy, d, len, opt} + L8.colony(seed, P, rounds) + L8.SNOW + L8.tenTau(round, i, j), L8.WHO + L8.VAR, L8.JOBS / JOB_IDS / evalOrder / SCHED / EDD.

B. DRAWING BASICS (common-3.js): L8.tag(parent, {x, y, text, tone, solid, fs, h}) -> {set({text, tone, solid, k, x, y, s, o}), el}; L8.chip(parent, {x, y, w, h, text, tone, fs, solid, radius}) -> {set({text, tone, solid, ghost, k, x, y, s, sx, o, ring, ringK}), el} (any rounded tile: a number, a letter, a unit block); L8.stat(parent, {x, y, w, h, label, tone}) -> set({text, tone, solid, bump, k, o, x, y}); L8.disc(parent, {x, y, size, text, tone}) (centre x, y); L8.token(parent, {tone, size}) -> set({x, y, s, o, tone}); L8.card(parent, {x, y, w, h, text, tone, plain, fs}); L8.label(parent, {x, y, w, text, tone, fs, align}) -> set({text, tone, k, x, y, o, bold}); SVG (append to your own L5.svg layer): L8.ant(x, y, size, tone) (an ant facing right; V.place(g, {x, y, r})), L8.mark(kind, x, y, size, tone) with kind 'times' | 'plus' | 'minus' | 'equals'; tools: L8.seq(t, t0, step, dur, i), L8.along(a, b, f, inset), L8.fit(nodes, box, pad), L8.tone(name), L8.TONES.

C. THE MAP (common-4.js): const net = L8.net(parent, {nodes: {id: [x, y] | {x, y, w, label}}, edges: [[a, b]], r, fs, roadW, labels, maxPaths, w, h}); net.update({roads, roadTone, tau (fn(a, b) | object | null), tauW: [w0, w1], tauNorm: {min, max, w0, w1, o0, o1}, tauK, tauTone, paths: [{a, b, k, tone, w, head, dash, o}], labels: {'A-B': {text, tone, solid, k}}, nodes: {id: {tone, solid, ring, ringK, ringDash, text, k, o, s, dy}}, nodeK, o}); net.pt(id), net.along(a, b, f, inset), net.walk(a, b, f) (where to draw the ant icon while it walks road a -> b), net.rest(id) (where it stands on a town); L8.ek(a, b) = road key.

D. CHARTS (common-5.js): const s = L8.strip(parent, {x, y, w, h, gap, max, fs}); s.update({parts: [{text, v, tone, solid}], k, ticks, marker: u, markerK, o}) -> {lefts, widths, markerX, cuts} (the share strip and roulette wheel with its random-number pointer); const b = L8.bar(parent, {x, y, w, h, tone, full}); b.set({v, tone, text, textIn, k, o, x, y}); const d = L8.dial(parent, {x, y, w, label, min, max, tone, fmt}); d.set({v, k, o, tone}) -> {knobX}; const g = L8.gantt(parent, {x, y, order, px, h}); g.update({n, dueK, lateK, tone, o}) -> {lefts, widths, rows, bottom} (the print shop's schedule: blocks, 'ends' / 'due' lines, late tags).

E. TIPS FOR SCENE AUTHORS. Tags, chips and stats set() every frame: pass k (0..1) to pop them in, o to fade them; a tag that has not popped yet must be set({k: 0}) every frame (otherwise it shows at full size). Chip offsets x, y are offsets from where the chip was placed (use them to fly a chip). Ants: put the icon on net.rest(town) or net.walk(a, b, f), never on the town centre (it would hide the letter). net.update draws grey base roads at 75 % opacity: pass roads: 0 where no base roads are wanted. The 45-road ten-village map is heavy to restyle every frame but fine (about 100 elements). A throwaway test scene is easiest with node tools/video-still.js <your-test-page> s2@4 <dir>; delete test pages before you finish. The stage is 936 x 640 and text never goes below 28 px; keep a 12 px margin.
